parts.markdown:
Use our free **Arkansas paycheck calculator** to estimate how much of your salary remains after federal income tax, Arkansas income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other payroll deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and customize your withholding information to see your estimated take-home pay.

Whether you work in Little Rock, Fayetteville, Bentonville, Fort Smith or another Arkansas community, knowing your estimated net income can help you compare employment opportunities, manage household expenses and establish realistic financial goals.

## How to Use the Arkansas Paycheck Calculator

Begin by entering your earnings before taxes and deductions.

If you receive a fixed salary, enter your annual gross compensation. Hourly employees should provide their hourly rate, regular hours and qualifying overtime hours.

Select your payment frequency. Enter federal and Arkansas income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Include any retirement contributions, health insurance premiums, additional withholding and other payroll deductions.

The calculator displays an estimated breakdown of individual deductions and remaining take-home earnings.

For the most accurate estimate, enter information from your latest pay stub and withholding certificates.

## Arkansas Payroll Taxes in 2026

Arkansas employees generally face federal and state income tax withholding alongside ordinary federal payroll contributions.

Arkansas reduced its highest individual income tax rate for the 2026 tax year. However, the original employer withholding instructions were issued before that legislative change.

Consequently, employees should distinguish between current payroll withholding and the income tax they ultimately owe when filing their annual return.

The [Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/) provides official tax information and employer resources.

## Understanding Arkansas Income Tax Withholding

Arkansas employers can calculate employee income tax withholding using official withholding tables or an authorized calculation formula.

The state provides withholding tables for different payroll frequencies.

An employee paid weekly may therefore have different withholding amounts per paycheck from an employee paid monthly, even when both receive the same annual salary.

The calculation also accounts for applicable withholding exemptions.

Do not estimate Arkansas income tax withholding by simply multiplying your entire gross salary by the highest state tax rate.

That approach ignores exemptions, deductions and the official payroll calculation methodology.

The original [2026 Arkansas employer withholding instructions](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/withholdInstructions_2026.pdf) explain the state's withholding framework. Check the Department of Finance and Administration for subsequent revisions.

## Arkansas Employee Withholding Certificates

Arkansas employees generally provide withholding information using Form AR4EC, the Employee's Withholding Exemption Certificate.

The form helps employers determine the applicable number of withholding exemptions.

Employees who qualify for special withholding exemption treatment may need to complete Form AR4ECSP instead.

Federal and Arkansas withholding certificates serve different purposes. Updating your federal Form W-4 does not necessarily update your Arkansas withholding elections.

Review your state withholding information after significant household changes, employment changes or other events that affect your expected tax liability.

Claiming fewer or more withholding exemptions can change your immediate paycheck without necessarily changing your final annual tax obligation.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Arkansas Paychecks

### Federal income tax

Federal income tax withholding depends on your taxable wages, filing status, payment frequency and Form W-4 adjustments.

Households with multiple jobs or other income sources may need additional withholding to align their payments with expected annual tax obligations.

Employers generally use the methods described in [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t).

### Social Security tax

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered Social Security wages.

For 2026, the annual taxable wage ceiling is $184,500.

An employee receiving $2,400 in covered earnings before reaching that annual limit would contribute $148.80.

### Medicare tax

Ordinary Medicare withholding is 1.45% of covered wages.

Unlike Social Security, ordinary Medicare does not have a standard annual taxable wage ceiling.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% on Medicare-covered wages exceeding $200,000 paid by that employer during the calendar year.

The [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) explains these requirements in greater detail.

## Arkansas Paycheck Example: $62,400 Annual Salary

Consider an Arkansas employee earning $62,400 annually.

Assume the employee receives $2,400 biweekly, with all wages covered by ordinary Social Security and Medicare contributions.

Social Security:

$2,400 × 6.2% = $148.80

Medicare:

$2,400 × 1.45% = $34.80

Total federal payroll contributions:

$148.80 + $34.80 = $183.60

The employee would have approximately $2,216.40 remaining before federal income tax, Arkansas income tax and other payroll deductions.

This example illustrates only part of the paycheck calculation.

Your actual net earnings depend on your withholding elections, benefit arrangements and other applicable adjustments.

## Arkansas Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can estimate gross earnings by multiplying their hourly wage by regular working hours and adding qualifying overtime compensation.

For example, an employee earning $23 per hour who works 40 regular hours and six qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half would receive:

Regular earnings:

$23 × 40 = $920

Overtime earnings:

$23 × 1.5 × 6 = $207

Total gross earnings:

$1,127

The applicable federal and Arkansas payroll deductions would then be calculated using the relevant taxable wage amounts.

Employees working in manufacturing, transportation, healthcare and retail may receive additional compensation through shift differentials, bonuses or overtime.

These earnings can cause paycheck amounts to vary throughout the year.

Review the [US Department of Labor overtime requirements](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) to understand overtime eligibility and applicable exemptions.

## Does Arkansas Have Local Income Taxes?

Arkansas municipalities generally do not impose a separate employee wage income tax.

This differs from states such as Ohio, where municipal and school district income taxes may significantly affect take-home pay.

However, local sales taxes and other household expenses can still affect your disposable income.

When comparing salaries in different Arkansas communities, consider housing, transportation, insurance and other essential expenses alongside your estimated paycheck.

These living expenses should be evaluated separately rather than deducted as payroll income taxes.

## Special Tax Considerations for Texarkana Residents

Arkansas has a special income tax exemption that may apply to qualifying residents of Texarkana, Arkansas, and certain income earned by qualifying Texas residents working in Texarkana, Arkansas.

This arrangement reflects the unusual geographic circumstances of a city located on the Arkansas–Texas border.

Eligibility depends on residency, income source and applicable state rules.

Do not assume that every person living or working near Texarkana automatically qualifies.

Employees claiming this treatment should confirm their eligibility with the Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration and their employer.

A standard statewide paycheck estimate may not fully represent these special arrangements.

## How Employee Benefits Affect Arkansas Take-Home Pay

Retirement contributions, health insurance premiums and other employee deductions can influence both your taxable wages and final paycheck.

Traditional 401(k) contributions generally reduce current federal income-taxable earnings, while Roth contributions generally do not provide the same immediate income tax reduction.

Certain qualifying health insurance arrangements may reduce applicable taxable wages.

Other deductions reduce the amount deposited into your bank account without necessarily reducing income or payroll taxes.

Review your pay stub to understand how each benefit is classified.

When comparing employment offers, consider employer retirement matching, insurance coverage and other benefits alongside your take-home salary.

## Planning Your Monthly Budget in Arkansas

Use estimated net income rather than gross salary when establishing a monthly spending plan.

Begin with essential expenses, including housing, groceries, transportation, utilities, insurance and debt payments.

Then determine how much you can allocate toward emergency savings, retirement and other financial objectives.

Employees paid biweekly should remember that most months contain two paychecks, while some contain three.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help estimate your savings requirements, while our [debt-to-income ratio calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) can help you evaluate your borrowing commitments.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the Arkansas state income tax rate in 2026?

Arkansas reduced its highest individual income tax rate to 3.7% for the 2026 tax year. Actual paycheck withholding depends on the applicable official payroll schedules and your withholding information.

### Does Arkansas deduct city income tax from paychecks?

Arkansas municipalities generally do not impose separate personal wage income taxes. Employees remain subject to applicable state and federal taxes.

### Can Texarkana residents qualify for an Arkansas income tax exemption?

Certain qualifying Texarkana residents and income arrangements may receive special state tax treatment. Confirm eligibility with the Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration before applying an exemption.
